1. ERROR PIPETTE-RANGE: 5 ul is below what the p300_single_gen2 can measure (20 ul at least)
   line 52:  p300.aspirate(5, well)
   At line 52 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 5 ul, below its minimum of 20 ul (this
   line did it 4 times). A pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the wrong
   amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The simulator
   passes the move. Wells: wells A1, B1, C1 and D1 in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, B1, C1 and D1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the
   reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.

6. WARNING MIX-TOO-WEAK: Mixing too weak to stir 20 wells: 2 × 5 ul in 90 ul
   line 68:  p300.aspirate(5, well)
   At line 68 the tip mixes wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B2, B3, B4 and 12 more in slot 3 with
   2 strokes of 5 ul in a well holding 90 ul (this line did it 20 times). 2 strokes of 5 ul
   move 0.11 of the well in all; it takes about 2 wells' worth of strokes to mix (the mixing
   work). Fewer than 3 strokes do not mix a well. Integra draws over 80% of the well five
   times; three mixes gave 11.8% CV where twenty gave 1.7%. What the well holds is not at
   the concentration you calculated, and in a dilution series every later step inherits the
   error.

   Fix: Mix the well with about 80% of its volume (72 ul) at least 5 times: `mix(5, 72,
   well)`. A stroke of the whole well draws air; use no more than 90%.
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide

   line 87:  p300.dispense(10, dest_well)
   At line 87 the robot added compound 1, dmso, compound 2, compound 3 and 1 more to wells
   A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 16 more in slot 4, which already held medium (this
   line did it 24 times). The addition was 10% of the well, nothing mixed the well
   afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do
   not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated.
   The liquid added last is a sample, so nothing else in the workflow will mix it: a
   normalisation or a pool left like this is not what it says it is.

   `mix_after=(5, 80)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 80, well)`, with the volume about
   80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to

   line 65:  p300.aspirate(30, prev_well)
   At line 65 the tip touched the liquid in wells A1, B1, C1 and D1 in slot 3 while it still
   carried dmso (well A1 in slot 5) from an earlier step (this line did it 4 times). A tip
   that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches. The
   protocol never transfers that liquid into these wells on purpose, so it was not meant to
   be there. If the wells hold different samples, each now holds a little of another. Liquid
   was later taken out of the affected wells, and the unwanted material went along into 4
   other wells: wells A1, B1, C1 and D1 in slot 4.
   Affected: wells A1, B1, C1 and D1 in slot 3.
   Also reached 4 other wells: wells A1, B1, C1 and D1 in slot 4.
   Fix: Use a fresh tip for each well at line 65. If one tip must serve many wells, dispense
   from above the liquid (for example `well.top()`) so that the tip never touches what is
   already in the well.

           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194

A pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the wrong amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The simulator passes the move. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 16 more in slot 3.
findings.fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.

findings.title: Mixing too weak to stir 20 wells: 2 × 5 ul in 90 ul
findings.explanation: At line 68 the tip mixes wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B2, B3, B4 and 12 more in slot 3 with 2 strokes of 5 ul in a well holding 90 ul (this line did it 20 times). 2 strokes of 5 ul move 0.11 of the well in all; it takes about 2 wells' worth of strokes to mix (the mixing work). Fewer than 3 strokes do not mix a well. Integra draws over 80% of the well five times; three mixes gave 11.8% CV where twenty gave 1.7%. What the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated, and in a dilution series every later step inherits the error.
findings.fix: Mix the well with about 80% of its volume (72 ul) at least 5 times: `mix(5, 72, well)`. A stroke of the whole well draws air; use no more than 90%.

findings.title: 24 wells never mixed after compound 1, dmso, compound 2, compound 3 and 1 more went in (10% of the well)
findings.explanation: At line 87 the robot added compound 1, dmso, compound 2, compound 3 and 1 more to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 16 more in slot 4, which already held medium (this line did it 24 times). The addition was 10% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. The liquid added last is a sample, so nothing else in the workflow will mix it: a normalisation or a pool left like this is not what it says it is.
findings.fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 16 more in slot 4 after line 87: `mix_after=(5, 80)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 80, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.

findings.title: No blank on a dilution series: 6 wells of compound 1
findings.explanation: At line 50 the robot starts a dilution series of compound 1 in NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 3): 6 wells at 6 concentrations, each level about 3 times weaker than the one before. No well on this plate holds dmso with no sample, so there is no blank: the curve has no zero to read against, and a signal from the diluent or the plastic cannot be told from the lowest point. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A6 in slot 3.
findings.fix: Add a well of dmso alone, and tell the plate map where it is.

findings.title: A used tip carried dmso (well A1 in slot 5) into 4 wells it was never meant for
findings.explanation: At line 65 the tip touched the liquid in wells A1, B1, C1 and D1 in slot 3 while it still carried dmso (well A1 in slot 5) from an earlier step (this line did it 4 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches. The protocol never transfers that liquid into these wells on purpose, so it was not meant to be there. If the wells hold different samples, each now holds a little of another. Liquid was later taken out of the affected wells, and the unwanted material went along into 4 other wells: wells A1, B1, C1 and D1 in slot 4.
findings.fix: Use a fresh tip for each well at line 65. If one tip must serve many wells, dispense from above the liquid (for example `well.top()`) so that the tip never touches what is already in the well.

findings.title: No blank on a dilution series: 6 wells of compound 1
findings.explanation: At line 87 the robot starts a dilution series of compound 1 in NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 4): 6 wells at 6 concentrations, each level about 3 times weaker than the one before. No well on this plate holds dmso and medium with no sample, so there is no blank: the curve has no zero to read against, and a signal from the diluent or the plastic cannot be told from the lowest point. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A6 in slot 4.
findings.fix: Add a well of dmso and medium alone, and tell the plate map where it is.
